testimony.witness_title: Member, Agua Caliente Band of Mission Indians
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Palm Springs reservation conditions, water rights, boundary disputes, airport lease money
testimony.key_claims: White neighbors encroaching on lands; old boundary lines lost; driven from Tahquitz Canyon by Agent McCallum; water company refused water rights despite pipeline crossing Indian land; Agent True refused Rogers' proposition for water; domestic water unfit with dead animals floating; airport taken with promise of payment but still waiting; $1,250.92 found by Dady but insufficient for water system; Indians willing to work for free to bring water

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Response to Agua Caliente Band complaints, survey visits, water project funding
testimony.key_claims: Visited Palm Springs more than any other reservation (7 times); found $1,250.92 airport money; engineer Rieger estimated $3,600 for pipe alone; asked office to cut down other reservation amounts to help them; requested $50,000 Public Works money for irrigation; Indians elected spokesmen; offered to get money for truck; claims Indians misinformed but have real heart

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.committee: Senate Committee on Indian Affairs, Subcommittee
testimony.subject: Indian land surveys, boundary disputes, resurvey vs. retracement issues
testimony.key_claims: Government sends eastern engineers who resurvey instead of retrace original lines; Indians cannot reconcile changes; should retrace original boundaries; Los Coyotes has four official government surveys of same line none found on ground; Lightfoot 1910 resurvey shifted boundary quarter mile; Indians have possessory rights under Spanish law; cemeteries within Spanish grants should be protected; General Land Office recapturing patented lands by resurvey; Churchill v. Beale and Choctaw Nation v. U.S. support compensation for survey mistakes

testimony.witness_title: Spokesman, Santa Ysabel Indian Reservation; Member, Mission Indian Federation
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Opposition to Wheeler bill, criticism of Commissioner Collier, Mission Indian Federation police charges
testimony.key_claims: Collier caused more dissension than any other Commissioner; Wheeler bill sets Indians back 100 years with own courts; Indians are voters and wish to continue as citizens; Collier claimed President appointed him without asking help; Mission Indian Federation police falsely accused of carrying guns; Mr. Moore refused to show telegram sent about charges

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Criticism of Commissioner Collier, Wheeler Bill, and Mesa Grande incident
testimony.key_claims: Commissioner Collier caused dissension with Wheeler Bill; Collier's statement about appointment was misleading; requested removal of employees; disputed Moore's telegram about armed Indians

testimony.witness_title: Special Officer, United States Indian Service
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Mesa Grande fiesta incident and telegrams to Commissioner
testimony.key_claims: Federation police carried concealed weapons; confrontation with 75 Indians demanding federal officers leave; comparison to Campo 1927 shooting; Robert Magee was discharged for inefficiency

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Federation police weapons at Mesa Grande fiesta
testimony.key_claims: Federation police not allowed to carry arms; Indians are peaceful people; requested Moore name which police were armed

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Mesa Grande fiesta August 5, 1933
testimony.key_claims: Did not encounter any armed Indian Federation policemen; no arrests made; fiesta went on peacefully; Moore's report was not true

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Mesa Grande fiesta and Moore's telegram
testimony.key_claims: Moore's telegram inaccurate; meeting with Willis and Prather was about school not Moore; federation police do not carry arms; Moore's report gave Mesa Grande a black name

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Moore's conduct at Mesa Grande fiesta
testimony.key_claims: Moore refused to show papers or explain authority; federation police appointed by people to maintain order; 95 percent of reservation members of federation; Willis and Prather advised truthfulness and law-abiding conduct

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Reservation boundaries, Court of Claims case, attorney representation, Indian police selection
testimony.key_claims: Old Indians never received true reservation lines; Government failed to show boundaries; Indians have big claim in Court of Claims for treaties; Attorney General Webb reduced claim from $12,800,000 to $6,000,000 without consulting Indians; Indians want own attorney not selected by Government; $6,000,000 only provides $250-300 per Indian; Indians should select own police; Government police disrespect Indians because Indians don't select or pay them

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Fiesta incident with Mr. Moore, alleged armed Indians
testimony.key_claims: Nicholas Chaparosa did not have gun and is not federation police; Denies 75 Indians gathered to chase officials out; Claims Moore only showed badge and card, refused to show proper papers; Claims Moore refused to work with fiesta committee; Claims Moore said he wouldn't work under nobody and would do what he pleased; Previous incidents with fake marshals harassing women

testimony.witness_title: Special Officer, Bureau of Indian Affairs
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Fiesta incident, law enforcement authority
testimony.key_claims: Offered to cooperate with fiesta committee but was refused; Committee told him to get off reservation; Threats of violence and mob scene occurred; Committee refused to allow him to make arrests or interfere with liquor sales; Arrested white man for bringing liquor on reservation; Read telegram from Commissioner Collier verifying authority

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Presence of arms at fiesta

testimony.hearing: Senate Committee on Indian Affairs consideration of S. 3572
testimony.subject: Opposition to allowing Indians private attorneys in Court of Claims case
testimony.key_claims: Stated that Collett and associates operated an organized racket since 1920; claimed AG Webb proceeded with due diligence and delays were caused by General Accounting Office; asserted recovery amount was predetermined at $6M (later revised to $13M in subsequent report); argued private attorneys would confuse case and reduce net judgment; stated Indians had no constitutional right to own attorneys in this suit; alleged Collett could not prove representation of 17,000 Indians

testimony.hearing: Senate Committee on Indian Affairs
testimony.subject: Support for S. 3572 and H.R. 7095 allowing Indian-chosen attorneys
testimony.key_claims: Revealed Commissioner's inconsistent estimates ($6M vs $13M vs $49M); alleged conspiracy to settle case for $6M without questioning book charges or acreage; argued Indians needed private attorneys to question set-offs and take testimony; stated AG Webb failed to challenge government charges; claimed Commissioner admitted value of treaty rights should be considered but wanted Department to determine value rather than testimony

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Representation of California Indians in Court of Claims
testimony.key_claims: Attorney General is handling case well; no need for private attorneys; per capita distribution would be a mistake; organizations have collected large sums unnecessarily since 1923 ($17K-$30K annually); case involves computation not controverted questions; three California Indian associations exist but no general organization; state has interest in rehabilitation

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: History of California Indian claims legislation and representation
testimony.key_claims: Initiated Raker bill in 1920; Attorney General delayed suit 15 months; original petition filed in error excluding many tribes; amendments delayed 2 years 7 months; Indians have constitutional right to attorneys of choice; amendments made 10 months after jurisdictional period expired; represents 17,000 Indians; opposed Secretary Fall in 1920s; per capita payment should be decided by future Congress

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: California Indians' Court of Claims case, attorney representation, and legislative history
testimony.key_claims: Represents 17,000 Indians; Court of Claims bill vetoed in 1926 and reintroduced; conflict with John Collier regarding investigation bill; suit filed 15 months late allowing 13 other cases priority; amendments filed after 3-year period may be jurisdictional problem; Indians should choose own attorneys; boundaries need to be traced and testimony taken before aged witnesses die; offsets should be checked by Indian attorneys

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Status of California Indians' Court of Claims case and accounting delays
testimony.key_claims: Accounting delays due to voluminous records and inability to have multiple accountants work simultaneously; suit filed within 15 months of 1920 act (well within 36-month deadline); no settlement of $6 million ever suggested; original complaint estimates $12 million recovery; rumors of $150 million recovery are unrealistic and unfortunate; opposes private attorneys selected by Collett but suggests if Congress amends bill to allow Indian-selected attorneys, State should withdraw entirely; amendments filed after 3 years may not be legally sustainable but recommends Congressional amendment to make safe; Blackfeet case resulted in deficiency judgment against Indians

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: California Indian claims prosecution
testimony.key_claims: Indians believe fabulous sums ($150M) recoverable; $14,000 remains of $15,000 appropriation; no objection to amendment allowing Indians to select attorneys; delays unfortunate for Indians; Federal Government negotiated treaties in ignorance; Indians moved from good lands to poorer lands; personal property never paid for

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Jurisdictional act amendment and Indian representation
testimony.key_claims: Jurisdictional act not broad enough to do justice; $1.25/acre limitation unfair; Indians entitled to value of land today if possessed since 1852; Court of Claims is congressional court; recovered $3.5M for Ute Indians by killing set-offs; Commissioner predetermined $6M judgment; need testimony on acreage, personal property value, and validity of set-offs; Indians alarmed by Office of Indian Affairs article

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Indian attorney selection
testimony.key_claims: Indians should have their own attorneys; it would be fairer and they would feel better

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Right to employ attorneys and delays
testimony.key_claims: Entitled to full privileges of employing attorney; 3-year limit exceeded (corrected by Chairman); money spent on attorneys but losing more in interest at 4% by not having judgment deposited

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Enrollment deficiencies
testimony.key_claims: Attorney general took 46 months to ascertain clients; several thousand Indians left out of petition; Robinson family in San Quentin left out; Congress should extend enrollment time 6 months; California Indians suffered longer than others

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Enrollment procedures
testimony.key_claims: Judge Raker made every effort to include everyone; final roll completed and approved by Secretary; time elapsed for accepting applications; cannot receive new applications

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Indian attorney representation
testimony.key_claims: Consensus of Indians is they want own attorneys; Indians intelligent and know white people have own attorneys; not satisfied with attorney general representing them; attorney general has Commonwealth interests to look after; under contract since 1928; willing to facilitate change of counsel if Indians desire

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Representation of California Indians in Court of Claims
testimony.key_claims: Indians unanimously want attorneys of their own choice; contract valid since 1928; Attorney General Webb refuses to associate with them due to prejudice against Collett; Indians have been robbed historically; testimony should have been taken long ago; Indians entitled to change attorneys if desired; Collett possesses essential information for the case

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Contract validity and attorney fees
testimony.key_claims: Contract entered 1928 after San Francisco convention with 24-26 delegates; fee structure is 2% on first $2M and 3% thereafter; willing to accept quantum meruit basis; engaged Washington counsel Esch, Kerr, Wooley, Taylor & Shipe; traveled extensively to Plumas County, Eureka, Butte County, Del Norte County; 17,000 Indians represented through 32 district auxiliaries; delays caused by Attorney General Webb; advice on one phase of case worth millions

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Opposition to private attorneys
testimony.key_claims: Attorneys do not represent 17,000 Indians (exaggerated, maybe 5,000); enrollment process misunderstood by Indians; no old Indians alive who know about 80-year-old treaties; no opposition to bill so no need for private attorneys; allowing free attorney selection would lead to bribery of group leaders; survey of reservations would be expensive; Senators' travel expenses charged against bill

testimony.witness: Unidentified witness (accompanied by Radke, Dimmick, Feree)
testimony.witness_title: Representative of D.A.R. or concerned citizen

testimony.subject: California Indians, Inc. meetings and solicitation of funds from destitute Indians
testimony.key_claims: Collett and Hanley stirred up dissatisfaction with State's Court of Claims representation; solicited $20,000 for private attorneys; Collett evaded questions about case readiness and money collected; Indians pressured to contribute despite destitution

testimony.subject: Klamath Reservation administration and violations of Public Act 435
testimony.key_claims: Crawford unqualified; two timber sales made in violation of Public Act 435 without general council consent; affidavits show people jailed for standing up for rights; young girl (Hull) handled roughly, jailed without matron, child died; morale broken; $30 million estate needs orderly administration

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in the United States
testimony.subject: Klamath timber sales and grazing lease irregularities
testimony.key_claims: Timber sold at $5.50 and $4.50 per thousand when stumpage worth $3; Weaver report shows high percentage merchantable timber vs. Zimmerman claim of 25%; Crawford allowed brother-in-law Crystal to graze sheep on Chiloquin Ridge before bidding opened; sheep brought back under Indian ownership via conditional sales to Crawford relatives

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in the United States (affidavit)
testimony.subject: Logging operations in beetle control camps
testimony.key_claims: Instructed to cut only logs 24-inch stump to 12-inch top; took all spike tops regardless of infestation; left bug-infested trees standing because too small; only cream of timber logged; no brush piling or treatment of infested butts; logs scaled after hauling to mill rather than on ground

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Beetle-control logging and grazing irregularities
testimony.key_claims: Beetle-control logging left merchantable timber standing; less than 25% merchantable timber per Zimmerman letter; Crawford improperly allowed Crystal to bring sheep onto reservation before bidding date; violation of Act 435; requested Weaver's report on logging
